did_you_know.text: Did you know? Ishmael son of Nethaniah is described as being of royal descent. He came to Gedaliah at Mizpah with ten men, and they ate bread together.
Did you know? After the meal, Ishmael and his ten men murdered Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
Did you know? The Jews who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah were also killed, along with the Chaldeans who were there.

Did you know? Eighty men from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria came mourning on their way to the house of the Lord. They had shaved their beards, torn their clothes, and brought grain offerings and incense.
Did you know? Ten of the captives pleaded with Ishmael not to kill them, offering him hidden provisions in the fields in exchange for their lives: wheat, barley, oil, and honey.
Did you know? The pit into which Ishmael threw the bodies of those he had killed was an old pit that King Asa had made because of Baasha king of Israel. Ishmael filled it with the dead.

Did you know? Ishmael took captive the rest of the people who remained at Mizpah, including the king’s daughters and the people whom Nebuzaradan had placed under Gedaliah’s care, and led them away toward the Ammonites.
Did you know? When the captives saw Johanan son of Kareah and the army commanders near Gibeon, they rejoiced and went toward them.
Did you know? Ishmael himself escaped from Johanan with only eight men and fled to the Ammonites.
Did you know? Johanan and the remnant of the people stopped near Bethlehem, by the lodging place of Chimham, because they were afraid of the Chaldeans and planned to continue on to Egypt.
